Odukoya, who described his decision to retain the recording as a grave mistake, also accused his sister and other family members who knew about the video of making it public.
He made the disclosure on Wednesday while addressing about 300 church workers amid the escalating leadership crisis rocking the church.
According to Church Times, Odukoya explained that his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, had requested that the video be recorded in 2021 before travelling to the United States for surgery.
He said the church founder, who feared he might not survive the operation, wanted to document his succession plans in case he died or became unable to communicate.
Jimmy said he personally recorded the message in which his father identified Areogun as the person who should take over the church’s leadership under such circumstances.
However, following his successful surgery, Taiwo reportedly instructed him to delete the recording, explaining that the circumstances that necessitated its creation had changed.
Rather than erase the video as directed, Jimmy retained it, a decision he now admits was wrong.
He further claimed that only a handful of people, including his sisters, knew about the recording before it became public, alleging that they were responsible for leaking it.
LEADERSHIP reposrts that the video has since become a major point of contention in the leadership crisis, with a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees relying on its contents to challenge Jimmy’s position as Senior Pastor.
On November 17, the faction announced the appointment of Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader of the church, citing Taiwo’s recorded instruction that Areogun should succeed him.
In the video, the late founder reportedly stated that Areogun should assume leadership if he died or became incapacitated, while Jimmy would serve as Areogun’s administrative assistant and head of the youth church.
Jimmy, however, has rejected the board faction’s decision, insisting that he remains the legitimate Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees.
He told the church workers that his disagreement with some board members began about a year after he assumed leadership following his father’s death.
According to him, the board members had asked him to relinquish his position as chairman and focus exclusively on his pastoral responsibilities.
He also alleged that his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, approached him with a similar request, seeking to have him step aside to allow her to become board chairman.
The disagreement reportedly escalated to the point where the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, was approached for intervention after Bishop Mike Okonkwo had earlier intervened.
Beyond the succession dispute, Jimmy also addressed allegations of financial misconduct, particularly claims that he misappropriated N250 million donated to the church for a project.
He denied the allegation, insisting that the money remained intact and that economic challenges were responsible for the delay in executing the project.
He also said he had restricted access to church funds, dismissing suggestions that he had engaged in financial impropriety.
Despite maintaining that he remains the church’s Senior Pastor, Jimmy reportedly expressed uncertainty over the conduct of the next Sunday service.
He also announced that an advertised church programme would not hold, explaining that the decision was intended to prevent further escalation of the leadership crisis.
